fields.acceptance: go test -trimpath ./internal/leftovers/... ./internal/adapter/... and go test -trimpath ./internal/api -run 'TestDaemonSweepLeftovers|TestRunLeftovers|TestSessionInterview|TestSessionAsk': a leftovers test records 3000 sessions (some of live runs) over a scratch tree of 1500 folders, counts directory reads through an injected reader or a counting wrapper, and asserts each scratch directory is read at most once while exactly the orphaned folders older than a day are removed and the freed bytes are counted; the claudecode test covers the scratch parents and session ID matching it now gives (no parents widened by an unsafe ID); TestDaemonSweepLeftoversPrunesOnlyOrphans still passes over the interview adapter's one-level $HOME/scratch/<sid> layout; a run's end still removes its sessions' scratch folders. Touches internal/leftovers/leftovers.go, internal/leftovers/leftovers_test.go, internal/adapter/adapter.go, internal/adapter/adapter_test.go, internal/adapter/claudecode/claudecode.go, internal/adapter/claudecode/claudecode_test.go, internal/api/daemon_leftovers.go, internal/api/daemon_leftovers_test.go, internal/api/run_leftovers.go, internal/api/session_interview_test.go, internal/api/session_ask_test.go
fields.statement: The leftovers sweep finds the session scratch folders to remove by listing each scratch level once per sweep and matching folder names against the recorded sessions of no live run, so its directory reads do not grow with the number of recorded sessions; what it removes and the line it logs are unchanged. The levels come from each adapter: the Adapter interface's ScratchGlobs gives way to a per-adapter list of scratch parents, glob patterns of the folders whose direct children are session folders named by session ID (Claude Code's <tmp>/claude-*/*, the interview test adapter's $HOME/scratch, none for the ask and adapter_test fakes), and the run-end cleanup in run_leftovers.go removes <parent>/<session ID> under the same parents

fields.acceptance: go test -trimpath ./internal/api -run 'TestPollGit': with a fake ctx.Start whose git never exits and a fake clock or a shortened limit, a test runs a project context's Git and GitConfig and asserts each returns an error naming the command and the limit after the limit, the program was killed, and a git that exits in time returns its output unchanged; a second test calls daemonHome with ctx.Root at the home project's own dir (so it returns that project's ctx, not a projectCtx) and the same fake ctx.Start, and asserts the home ctx's Git and GitConfig the poll uses are bounded the same way, not the caller's unbounded Git. Touches internal/api/daemon_projects.go, internal/api/daemon.go, internal/api/daemon_projects_test.go
fields.statement: Every git program the daemon's poll runs through a project's context (the home project's Git and each other project's Git and GitConfig) is killed after 30 s with GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0, as execWithin does for the model-branch work, and fails with an error naming the git command and the time limit, so a hung git costs a poll at most that long per call; the self-update's make and the run drivers the poll detaches are not bounded
